# Wormkey

> Wormkey creates temporary public URLs for software running on localhost. It is designed for developer previews, browser testing, webhook debugging, human handoffs, and AI-agent workflows.

Website: https://wormkey.run
Repository: https://github.com/max-pantom/worm
NPM CLI: https://www.npmjs.com/package/wormkey
NPM MCP server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wormkey/mcp
Current release: 0.4.0

## Primary documentation

- Agent guide: https://github.com/max-pantom/worm/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md
- CLI reference: https://github.com/max-pantom/worm/blob/main/docs/CLI.md
- Tunnel protocol: https://github.com/max-pantom/worm/blob/main/docs/PROTOCOL.md
- Releases: https://wormkey.run/release

- Blog: https://wormkey.run/blog
- Agent-native release story: https://wormkey.run/blog/wormkey-0-4-agent-native

## Quick start

Install:

    npm install --global wormkey@0.4.0

Expose localhost:

    wormkey http 3000

Machine-readable tunnel:

    wormkey http 3000 --json --no-interactive

Wait for readiness:

    wormkey http 3000 --wait-for /health --timeout 60s --json --no-interactive

Manage application and tunnel together:

    wormkey run --port 3000 --wait-for /health -- npm run dev

## Agent operations

- List tunnels: `wormkey list --json`
- Read status: `wormkey status <session-or-slug> --json`
- Close remotely: `wormkey close <session-or-slug> --json`
- Capture requests: `wormkey http 3000 --inspect`
- Read request logs: `wormkey logs --json`
- Inspect one request: `wormkey inspect <request-id>`
- Replay locally: `wormkey replay <request-id>`
- Create restricted token: `wormkey token create <session> --name <name> --scope tunnel:connect,tunnel:read --max-ttl 2h`

## MCP

Install:

    npm install --global @wormkey/mcp@0.4.0

Start:

    wormkey-mcp

Tools:

- `wormkey_start_tunnel`
- `wormkey_get_tunnel`
- `wormkey_list_tunnels`
- `wormkey_close_tunnel`
- `wormkey_get_requests`
- `wormkey_replay_request`
- `wormkey_wait_until_ready`

## JSON tunnel output

The `--json --no-interactive` command writes one object to stdout:

    {
      "session_id": "sess_123",
      "url": "https://quiet-lime-k7m4.wormkey.run",
      "owner_url": "https://wormkey.run/.wormkey/owner?slug=quiet-lime-k7m4&token=...",
      "expires_at": "2026-07-25T21:00:00.000Z",
      "pid": 4821,
      "status": "connected"
    }

Status messages are written to stderr.

## Security

- Wormkey uses an outbound tunnel from the CLI to the edge gateway.
- Public, owner, and internal control-plane APIs have separate authorization boundaries.
- Owner and tunnel credentials are stored as hashes by the control plane.
- Treat owner URLs, owner tokens, session tokens, and restricted tokens as secrets.
- Use short expiration times and close tunnels when work is complete.
- Request inspection stores request metadata locally and should only be enabled when appropriate.

## Product boundary

Wormkey is not permanent hosting or a deployment platform. It is a temporary handoff layer between local execution and external reviewers, browsers, services, and AI agents.
